challenges.name: bounded-queue-backpressure-quiz
challenges.title: What does a full queue do to the producer?
challenges.description: A bounded queue is only useful if you know what happens at its edges: when it is full, when it is empty and when it is closed.

questions.explanation: push() resolves immediately for the first two thumbnails because the queue has room. The third push() returns a promise that stays pending until a consumer pulls, so the loop is suspended at that await: 'queued' is logged twice, and the producer stops creating thumbnails. At most three blobs exist - two in the buffer and the one waiting inside the pending push(). That pause is backpressure: memory is bounded by the capacity instead of by the number of files. Nothing is dropped and nothing throws; a full queue is a normal state, not an error.

options.text: All 5 are queued; the queue drops the two oldest thumbnails to stay at capacity 2.
'queued' is logged twice; the third push() stays pending, so the loop pauses until a consumer pulls - at most three thumbnails exist.
The third push() throws a QUEUE_FULL error, and the loop ends with an unhandled rejection.
All 5 are logged as 'queued' immediately; capacity only limits how many items a consumer can pull at once.

questions.question: The user leaves the chat while uploads are still queued, and the app calls queue.close(). Which behaviours make close() safe for a producer/consumer queue? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Closing means "no new items", not "throw away what was accepted": items already in the queue are still delivered, and consumers see the end of the stream ({ done: true }) only after it is drained - otherwise accepted uploads vanish silently. A consumer waiting on an empty queue must be woken with { done: true }, or its for await loop hangs forever and leaks whatever it holds. A push() after close() is a programming error or a race the producer must learn about, so it should reject rather than drop the item quietly. And the end of the stream is a normal outcome: rejecting pending pulls would force every consumer to treat a clean shutdown as a failure.

options.text: Items already in the queue are still delivered; consumers get { done: true } only after the queue has drained.
A consumer that is waiting in pull() on an empty queue is woken with { done: true } instead of waiting forever.
push() after close() resolves quietly and discards the item, so producers never need error handling.
close() rejects every pending pull() with an error, so consumers notice the shutdown faster.

challenges.name: bounded-async-queue
challenges.title: Build a bounded async queue
challenges.description: Write createAsyncQueue({ capacity }) with push(item) (resolves when there is room), pull() (resolves with { value, done: false } or waits while empty), close() (accepted items still drain, then { done: true }; push after close rejects with QUEUE_CLOSED) and [Symbol.asyncIterator] for for await consumers. The harness interleaves producers and consumers step by step and logs exactly when each push and pull settles.

tests.name: push resolves at once while there is room; pull returns items in FIFO order
A full queue makes push wait until a consumer pulls
pull waits while the queue is empty and receives the next pushed item
close: accepted items still drain, then done; push after close is rejected
close wakes waiting consumers and ends a for await consumer
